findings.title: No-clobber archive needs hard links and fails where the old mv worked, leaving a closed review's state live
findings.problem: archive() moves a file with os.link + os.unlink and has no fallback. os.link fails with EPERM/ENOTSUP/EXDEV, not FileExistsError, on filesystems without hard-link support: exFAT/FAT32 external drives, many SMB/AFP/NFS and FUSE mounts, and some container bind mounts. The OSError reaches main() and the script exits 1. The old `mv` is a rename(2) inside one directory and works on all of those. 90-finalize.md runs the state archive (line 60) and both REVIEW.md archives (lines 216, 226) without checking the exit code. So on such a filesystem the state file stays at $STATE_FILE after an APPROVED REVIEW.md is written, the next /review carries the closed review forward instead of starting fresh, and a prior REVIEW.md from another phase that is no longer archived gets overwritten by the Write. pending: confirm on one such mount (for example a repo on an exFAT volume) that os.link raises and finalize then leaves `<state>.json` unarchived.
findings.fix_hint: on a non-FileExistsError OSError from os.link, fall back to an O_CREAT|O_EXCL copy then unlink (still no-clobber); have 90-finalize check the helper's exit code and stop with the uncertain message instead of reporting success
findings.why_it_matters: Every 2.12.0 user runs this code path on every --finalize. Users whose repo sits on a filesystem without hard links get a review that reports closed but whose state never archives, and that failure is silent.

findings.title: Finalize archive fences ignore review_archive.py exit status and print success text unconditionally
findings.problem: The unstamped branch runs `review_archive.py unstamped` and then always echoes 'archived aside as REVIEW-unstamped-<date>.md'. The review-md branch and the state archive bullet (line 60) also never test the exit code. The helper now has failure exits the old mv lacked (1 on a link error or when 1000 names are taken, 2 on usage). Unlike every other step in this file, which halts with 'nothing was written or archived', these fail open. The old mv was also unchecked, so the gap was partly there before, but the new helper widens the ways it can fail. pending: a run where the helper exits non-zero and the REVIEW.md write still proceeds.
findings.current_code:
python3 "$VC_ROOT/scripts/review_archive.py" unstamped --dir .turingmind
  echo "An earlier REVIEW.md was written by a plugin version that does not read this review's state; archived aside as REVIEW-unstamped-<date>.md — it did not close this review."
findings.fix_hint: wrap each review_archive.py call in `if ! ...; then echo uncertain...; exit 1; fi`, as the other finalize fences do
findings.why_it_matters: A failed archive followed by the REVIEW.md Write destroys the prior report, which is the loss this change was written to prevent.

findings.title: Frozen run_case.sh hard-codes Phase-54 memory-park and transcript paths, so later windows break unless a new manifest is issued
findings.problem: run_case.sh takes RUNBOOK from the environment, and its README says later-window runbooks will be built from RUN-PHASE54-live.md. But the post-run memory move reads the hard-coded `$HOME/.b3/phase54-live-memory-park.env`, not the runbook's MEMPARK_ENV. The NVW grep reads the hard-coded `runs-phase54-live/` (line 106). In a Phase-55 window that env file may not exist, PD is then empty and `mv "$M" "/$CP-written-..."` targets the filesystem root. That fails under `set +e`, so the clone's auto-memory is left in place, which is the known measurement confound. The next pre block's mem_evidence partly mitigates this. The directory is in freeze_manifest.COVERED, so fixing it after freeze is an identity change that needs a new manifest.
findings.fix_hint: use $MEMPARK_ENV and $ARCHIVE from the runbook's common block, and refuse when PD is empty, before the Phase-55 manifest is issued
findings.why_it_matters: Phase 55 measurement depends on this runner. A late fix forces a manifest reissue, and an unfixed one risks auto-memory contaminating measured runs.

findings.title: Placeholder NV strip turns a fresh symbol-anchored record with line null into a normal finding with no line
findings.problem: _nv_marked looks only at trigger/path/consequence, never at `symbol`. A fresh record with `line: null`, `needs_verification.symbol` set and placeholder fields (30-collect-score.md:60 describes this shape) used to be dropped as nv-not-admitted. Now the key is stripped and the record enters normal scoring, site grouping and render with line None, which the normal-finding path was never built for. pending: run score.run on such a record and check the row renders and hashes without error and without a `file:None` location.
findings.fix_hint: keep the drop path, or require line >= 1, for a stripped record that has no usable line
findings.why_it_matters: This is an edge case but it ships to every user, and score.py output feeds both state and render.

agent_notes: Scope read: all of area6 (plugin), the area5 runner layer (common.sh, run_case.sh, settings), the fix-harness source diffs (fixharness, harness_sandbox, harness_seed, harness_verdict, harness_record, driver), and holdout_autopilot/holdout_kit. The ~10K lines of new freeze-kit source and tests (freeze_check, freeze_manifest, freeze_policy, semgrep_replica) and holdout_eval_launch were only skimmed via the stat. They are measurement tooling, not shipped, and their tests are green (freeze 308, holdout 1169, harness 460).

What ships to users: plugin.json 2.12.0, score.py placeholder normalization, review_archive.py plus the 90-finalize routing, and one schema/scoring prose sentence. Nothing else in this range reaches user installs. replay.py's new DIFF_ROOTS entry is a repo-relative docs path that only the dev replay tool uses.

score.py blast radius: the new branch only fires for a FRESH record whose needs_verification dict has no real field. Carried NV rows are untouched (nv_carried_ids check comes first), and records without the key are byte-identical. The guardrail/replay report shows no archived envelope moved, consistent with older lanes never emitting placeholder NV dicts. Effect: findings that used to vanish as nv-not-admitted (dict {} or 'N/A'/'none'/'-') now score normally under their own agent_confidence, so expect slightly more visible findings from lanes that fill every schema key. That is the intended D-28 direction. A record with one real field and two placeholders still drops (tested). The whole-field match avoids eating prose such as 'none of the callers'.

agent-output-schema.md is read by all 11 review lanes. The added sentence is additive guidance and changes no required field, so lane parsing is unaffected. Behavior changes only when a lane starts writing placeholders, which score.py now absorbs safely.

Archive-name compatibility: the `-N` suffix stays compatible with every reader I found. 05-state.md:28 uses `find -name "<state>.archived-*"`, which matches `-2`. harness_verdict._archived_states globs `*.json.archived-*`. No reader parses the date out of the name. The same-phase change (a stamped REVIEW.md is now always archived) adds one small file per re-finalize under .turingmind/. Growth is unbounded in principle but negligible, and the directory is gitignored.

review_archive.py's TOCTOU handling (link fails when the target exists, then re-select) is sound for no-clobber. The weak spot is portability (imp-001): hard links are a stronger filesystem requirement than the rename that `mv` used, and no fallback exists.

Fix-harness: snapshot_plugin_from_commit now materializes the plugin from git objects (ls-tree + cat-file --batch). It refuses symlinks and odd modes and blocks path traversal, which is a real tightening against working-tree contamination. The probe default candidate is HEAD, documented as capability-only. The new undecided_nv term in _outstanding means a harness run that leaves NV items undecided now FAILS where it used to pass, which is intended. Legacy-location state is a named failure, not a fallback.

Holdout autopilot: freeze_identity runs on every _launch after _assert_journaled. An identity stop therefore leaves a journaled session id that was never launched. Worth confirming that resume logic doesn't treat a journaled-but-unlaunched id as a live session. That is a measurement-tooling question only, no user impact.

Multi-process: review_archive is safe against concurrent finalize (os.link EEXIST loop). Two finalizes on the same state at once would still both write REVIEW.md, but only one link+unlink of the state succeeds and the other exits 1, made silent by imp-002. This was equally racy before.
Performance: nothing scale-relevant. _nv_value adds O(3) string ops per NV-keyed record; archive_name is linear in same-day archive count.

Verdict: 2.12.0 is shippable. No breaking API or schema change. imp-001/imp-002 (finalize archive portability and unchecked exits) are the only user-facing risks and are bounded to non-hard-link filesystems. Fix imp-003 before issuing the Phase-55 manifest, because the runner directory is frozen.
